## JNJ Quantitative Fundamental Assessment — 2026-05-15

### 1. Revenue, Earnings, Margin & Cash-Flow Trajectory

**Revenue** is growing at a decelerating pace. Sequential quarters: Q1 21.89B → Q2 23.74B (+8.5%) → Q3 23.99B (+1.1%) → Q4 24.06B (+0.3%). TTM revenue is 93.69B. Top-line momentum has essentially stalled at ~24B/quarter.

**Earnings** tell a more complicated story. Q1 (period_end 2025-03-30) reported EPS of 4.54 — more than double the subsequent three quarters (2.29, 2.12, 2.14). Operating income in Q1 was 13.63B on just 21.89B of revenue, implying a 62.3% operating margin — an obvious one-time gain (likely a divestiture or legal recovery). Stripping this, the trailing three quarters' operating income totals 19.97B (~6.66B/quarter annualized to ~26.6B), far below the reported TTM of 33.60B. Normalized EPS runs approximately 2.18/quarter (mean of Q2–Q4), or ~8.72 annualized.

**Margins** are compressing. Latest-quarter gross profit declined 4.4% QoQ despite a revenue increase, implying cost-of-revenue rose from 7.30B (Q3) to 8.11B (Q4) — an 11.1% jump. Operating margin fell from 31.2% (Q3) to 24.9% (Q4). Net margin at the latest ratio observation is 21.8%, down from 24.4% a year ago.

**Cash generation** is the most alarming datapoint. Latest-quarter operating cash flow was 2.51B, down 72.6% from Q3's 9.17B and the weakest quarter in the four-quarter window. TTM operating cash flow is 19.73B — adequate on the surface, but the trajectory is deteriorating sharply. Free cash flow is unavailable.

### 2. Earnings Quality & Balance-Sheet Resilience

The Q1 distortion (EPS=4.54, operating_margin=62.3%, cash=38.78B) materially flatters all TTM figures. After adjusting, normalized quarterly earnings power is roughly 2.1–2.3 EPS, or ~8.7 annualized — meaning the stock is not as cheap on "true" earnings as headline TTM metrics suggest.

The balance sheet is sound: total equity of 81.19B, cash of 22.05B, and total liabilities of 119.71B. The debt-to-equity ratio is 1.47x — manageable for a healthcare conglomerate with stable demand. Cash declined from 38.78B in Q1 (inflated by the same one-time event) to the 18–22B range in subsequent quarters, which is the normal run-rate. No solvency concern.

### 3. Valuation Versus Own History

This is where the case becomes most uncomfortable. On a 365-day lookback:

| Metric | Current | 365d Low | Position in Range |
|---|---|---|---|
| P/E (diluted) | 26.82x | 16.63x | **Maximum** |
| P/B | 6.95x | 4.64x | 85th percentile |
| Earnings yield | 3.7% | — | **Below 10Y Treasury (4.47%)** |
| Net margin | 21.8% | 20.0% | Near bottom of range |
| ROE | 25.9% | 25.0% | Near bottom of range |

The P/E has expanded 61% from 16.6x (May 2025) to 26.8x today — the widest multiple in the entire observation window — while net margin has *contracted* from 24.4% to 21.8% and ROE from 27.9% to 25.9%. The market is paying a historically peak multiple for a business whose profitability is declining. An earnings yield of 3.7% against a 10-year Treasury yield of 4.47% means the equity is yielding less than risk-free — a rarity for JNJ and a clear overvaluation signal on a fundamental basis.

### 4. Price Context

The stock closed at 230.80 on 2026-05-14, within a 365-day range of 147.33–251.71 (91.7% of the high). The quarterly path shows a massive rally: +11.1% (Aug–Nov 2025), +26.2% (Nov 2025–Feb 2026), then a –5.6% pullback in the latest quarter. Price has already captured and overshot the fundamental trajectory; the recent decline may be the beginning of mean reversion toward fair value.

### 5. Macro & Sentiment Overlays

**Macro** is broadly headwind. The 10-year Treasury yield has climbed from 4.05% to 4.47% over 90 days (+10.4%), directly compressing the relative attractiveness of JNJ's 3.7% earnings yield. WTI crude has surged 67% to $104.66/bbl — a material cost-of-revenue headwind for a manufacturer, consistent with the gross-margin pressure visible in Q4. Breakeven inflation has risen to 2.47% from 2.26%, and the corporate Baa spread is at 6.09%, modestly wider. The only supportive macro datapoint is the VIX decline to 17.26 from a March peak of 31, indicating calmer markets — but this does not offset the fundamental and valuation negatives.

**News sentiment** is neutral-to-mildly positive (mean score 0.548 across 97 articles). No material directional signal; this is noise, not thesis.

### 6. Strongest Quantitative Upside & Downside

**Upside:** TTM operating cash flow of 19.73B is robust even if the latest quarter was weak, and the balance sheet carries 22.05B of cash with no solvency risk. If margins stabilize and the Q1 gain was a harbinger of portfolio simplification unlocking value, the stock has defensive characteristics. The 25.9% ROE remains solid.

**Downside:** The P/E of 26.82x sits at the absolute ceiling of its 365-day range while normalized EPS power (~8.7 annualized) implies a fair-value P/E-adjusted price far below 230. A reversion to even the midpoint P/E of ~21.5x on normalized EPS of ~8.7 implies a price near 187 — a ~19% drawdown. The –72.6% QoQ OCF collapse and +11.1% QoQ cost-of-revenue spike suggest margin erosion is accelerating, not stabilizing. Rising rates provide a persistent headwind to the multiple.

### 7. Provisional Conclusion

**Fundamentally unattractive.** JNJ's core business is exhibiting decelerating revenue growth, margin compression (gross profit –4.4% QoQ, cost-of-revenue +11.1% QoQ), and sharply weakening cash generation (OCF –72.6% QoQ). An anomalous Q1 quarter inflates all TTM metrics. Against this backdrop, the stock trades at a record-high 26.8x P/E — the widest in its 365-day window — with an earnings yield (3.7%) below the risk-free rate (4.47%). The price has already run 57% off its 365-day low, front-running fundamentals that are now deteriorating. The macro regime (rising rates, surging oil costs, widening credit spreads) compounds the risk. Quantitatively, the risk-reward is skewed to the downside at current levels.

# Johnson & Johnson (JNJ) — Qualitative Franchise Assessment
**Decision Date: 2026-05-15**

---

## 1. Business / Franchise Read

Johnson & Johnson is a streamlined two-pillar healthcare franchise — **Innovative Medicine (~65% of revenue)** and **MedTech (~35%)** — following the 2023 Kenvue consumer-health spin-off. The structural web_search evidence consistently describes JNJ as holding **#1 or #2 market share** in the majority of categories it competes in and maintaining a **AAA-rated balance sheet**, one of only two U.S.-based companies with that distinction. The franchise is built on three durable moats: deep intellectual property across disease areas, global commercial scale (hospitals, retail pharmacies, government health programs in 175+ countries), and switching costs embedded in physician workflows and chronic-treatment protocols.

In **Innovative Medicine**, the portfolio spans oncology, immunology, neuroscience, cardiovascular/metabolism, pulmonary hypertension, and infectious diseases. The company has **28 distinct products/platforms generating over $1 billion in annual sales**. The newer anchors — Darzalex (multiple myeloma, "$14B+ annually"), Carvykti (CAR-T cell therapy), Tremfya (immunology, "growing 40% in 2025 to reach $5.15 billion"), and Rybrevant/Lazcluze — are replacing the maturing Stelara franchise. JNJ has set an explicit goal of becoming **the #1 oncology company by 2030 with over $50 billion in oncology sales**.

In **MedTech**, the acquisitions of Abiomed (2022, heart recovery) and Shockwave Medical (2024, intravascular lithotripsy) have repositioned the division around high-growth cardiovascular, electrophysiology, and surgical robotics. MedTech offers more stable, procedure-driven recurring revenue (consumables, replacement cycles, installed-base pull-through) that is less dependent on patent cycles than pharma. The Ottava robotic surgical system is advancing through clinical trials (OTAVA trials for US FDA de novo submission).

The revenue trajectory confirms execution: FY2025 reported sales of **$94.2 billion (+6.0% YoY)**, and Q1 2026 revenue of **$24.06 billion (+9.9% YoY)**, with the company guiding to approximately **$100.5 billion** in 2026 revenue (5.7–6.7% growth). Morningstar's structural analysis notes returns on invested capital "in the midteens or even approach 20%, well above our estimated 7.2% cost of capital," supporting the wide economic moat characterization. The company has increased its dividend for **over 60 consecutive years**, recently raising the quarterly payout to **$1.34 per share** (annualized $5.36, ~2.3% yield).

## 2. Recent Developments (Dated)

**Q1 2026 earnings (reported April 14, 2026):** Adjusted EPS of $2.70 beat consensus of $2.68 by $0.02; revenue of $24.06B beat the $23.60B estimate. Innovative Medicine revenue grew 11.2% operationally; MedTech grew 7.7%. The company raised FY2026 guidance to EPS of $11.45–$11.65 and revenue of $100.3–$101.3B. *(Sources: ad-hoc-news.de 2026-05-11; dailypolitical.com 2026-05-08)*

**Dividend increase (May 2026):** Quarterly dividend raised from $1.30 to $1.34, payable June 9, 2026, signaling management confidence in cash generation. *(Source: dailypolitical.com 2026-05-08)*

**Product pipeline advances (May 2026):** JNJ launched the **Shockwave C2 Aero Coronary IVL Catheter** globally, expanding the cardiovascular device portfolio. Clinical and commercial progress in cardiology, Crohn's disease, and the OTTAVA robotic surgical system was also noted. *(Source: finance.yahoo.com, May 2026)*

**Institutional activity (Q4 2025):** Western Wealth Management increased its JNJ position by 14.5% to 17,600 shares. Larger holders (Vanguard, BlackRock, State Street) remain significant positions. *(Source: dailypolitical.com 2026-05-08)*

**CVS biosimilar expansion (2026-05-06):** CVS announced plans to expand biosimilar adoption in formularies starting July 1, 2026, prioritizing lower-cost alternatives — a relevant headwind for JNJ's remaining branded portfolio exposure.

## 3. Material Risks and Offsets

**Stelara biosimilar erosion (confirmed, structural):** Stelara, previously JNJ's largest drug (~$10B franchise), is experiencing "significant decline in revenue" due to biosimilar competition following loss of exclusivity. This is the single largest quantifiable revenue headwind. *Offset:* Q1 2026 results show Innovative Medicine grew 11.2% despite Stelara decline, indicating newer products (Darzalex, Carvykti, Tremfya, Rybrevant/Lazcluze, Spravato) are more than compensating. Structural sources note 11.5% operational growth in 2025 excluding Stelara.

**Talc litigation overhang (confirmed, unquantified):** Multiple structural sources describe the talc litigation as a "persistent risk" and "unquantifiable talc litigation overhang." No resolution timeline is evident. *Offset:* The AAA balance sheet and substantial cash flow generation provide a buffer; the company has been proactively managing the liability through settlements and legal strategy.

**IRA pricing pressure (confirmed, emerging):** The Inflation Reduction Act creates negotiating pressure on key drugs including Xarelto. *Offset:* Specialty and newer-launch drugs tend to carry stronger pricing power and face lower regulatory hurdles; the portfolio is shifting toward these categories.

**MedTech competitive intensity (inferred):** Orthopedics is described as "struggling to maintain share against more focused players like Stryker and Zimmer Biomet." In robotic surgery, Ottava faces entrenched competition from Intuitive Surgical's da Vinci platform. In electrophysiology, JNJ lacks a PFA (pulsed field ablation) product in the U.S., though it benefits from procedural volume increases driven by PFA adoption. *Offset:* Cardiovascular (Shockwave, Abiomed) and electrophysiology (CARTO) are growing strongly; the dual-pillar model provides diversification.

**Macro/regulatory uncertainty:** China VBP (volume-based procurement) impacting MedTech margins; currency headwinds; general healthcare cost containment trends are cited in JNJ's own risk disclosures.

## 4. Qualitative Assessment

**Assessment: Positive — the narrative supports fundamental attractiveness.**

JNJ presents a structurally durable, defensively-positioned franchise that is executing a credible portfolio transition. The dual-pillar model (Innovative Medicine + MedTech) provides genuine diversification that pure-play peers lack: when pharma faces patent cliffs, procedure-driven MedTech offers stability, and vice versa. The evidence shows the Stelara headwind — the most material near-term risk — is being absorbed by accelerating growth in oncology, immunology, and cardiovascular devices. Q1 2026's 9.9% revenue growth and raised full-year guidance demonstrate the transition is working at scale.

The franchise quality is high: AAA credit rating, 60+ year dividend streak, #1/#2 market positions, $32B+ annual R&D and acquisition capacity, and 28 billion-dollar products. The oncology ambition ($50B by 2030) and MedTech robotics roadmap (Ottava, Shockwave, electrophysiology) provide multi-year structural growth vectors beyond simple organic replacement.

The primary qualification is that the talc litigation remains an unresolved, unquantified overhang that constrains valuation sentiment despite strong operational execution. However, for a fundamental-qualitative view, the franchise's durability, capital-allocation discipline, and proven ability to navigate patent transitions through pipeline and M&A make JNJ a credible long-duration holding. A good quarter does not make the franchise, but here the quarter confirms a structural trend already well-evidenced in the business model.
